fields.v: Bondarenko, A., Zamorskaia, N., Djakons, D., Djakona, A., Djakons, R. (2026). Control-Plane Placement and Memory Substrates in Modern Agentic AI: A Comparative Method for Prompt-Native Systems, Agent Shells, and Durable Runtimes. Latvian Journal of Physics and Technical Sciences, 2026(5), 46-64. DOI: 10.2478/lpts-2026-0036
Journal — Latvian Journal of Physics and Technical Sciences, 2026, N 5
Riga Nordic University, Latvia (all authors)

Conceptual; secondary: Proposes an evaluation method — document-based qualitative comparison of five agentic system families / 12 coding agents; proposes a control-plane placement comparative method (L/M/H coding matrix, rubric), a benchmark-interpretation formula and a disclosure checklist
fields.why: Main nature is a judgement: the title and the three stated contributions (p 2-3) are a comparative method, so 'Proposes an evaluation method' (or 'Compares', document-based) as main is defensible. If the documentation-based coding of 12 tools were read as an empirical qualitative study, Q3-Q8 would apply instead of N/A.

fields.v: No single SDD approach. Five control-plane families: prompt-native packs (Superpowers, SKILL.md bundles, prompt collections); prompt-modular shells (Cline v3, KiloCode); runtime-governed shells (Claude Code, OpenCode, Qwen Code, Gemini CLI, Warp); host-mediated/coordinator forms (GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf, Kiro); durable workflow runtimes (LangGraph, Vertex AI ADK, OpenAI Codex). Kiro noted for 'specs as source-of-truth control artefacts'. Versions not stated (evidence as of early/mid 2026)
